title: Manic Android Malware Steals Banking PINs and Takes Remote Control of Devices
content_md: A newly identified Android malware family dubbed Manic combines banking fraud, spyware, and remote-access capabilities in a single platform. ThreatFabric’s Mobile Threat Intelligence team says the threat is notable for an uncommon peer-relay mechanism that can exfiltrate stolen data via nearby compromised phones when a victim device lacks a direct internet connection. Manic has been active since at least February 2026, with infrastructure and development activity expanding through spring. Manic Android Malware Steals Banking PINs By July, operators had introduced a more advanced build featuring stronger anti-analysis checks, in-memory DEX loading, and lock-screen credential phishing . The malware monitors 169 Android package IDs across banking, payment, cryptocurrency, government identity, authentication, email, browser, and messaging applications. Data stealer and Device Takeover (DTO) Flow (Source: Threat Fabric) Ukraine appears to be the primary target, with coverage of Ukrainian banks, eID services, and messaging tools. However, its target list also includes services used in Russia, Poland, Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, the UK, and other European countries, as well as global fintech and crypto platforms. Unlike conventional Android banking trojans, Manic does not always rely on a full-screen fake login overlay to steal credentials. Instead, it can abuse Android Accessibility permissions to place a transparent layer over the numeric keypad inside a legitimate bank
